nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, a finite sequence $(x_1, \ldots, x_m)$ of natural numbers is block-compatible for $n$ when $x_1 \ge x_2 \ge \cdots \ge x_m$, every $x_k$ satisfies $2 \le x_k \le n$, and there is a pairwise balanced design on the point set $\{0, \ldots, n - 1\}$ whose blocks, listed in order as $B_1, \ldots, B_m$, have sizes $|B_k| = x_k$ for every $k$.
nodes.title: Block-compatible sequences

nodes.summary: There are a real number $c > 0$ and a natural number $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$ there is a finite set of at least $\exp(c \sqrt{n} \log n)$ distinct finite sequences of natural numbers, each of which is block-compatible for $n$. Here $\log$ is the natural logarithm.
nodes.title: Many block-compatible sequences (Erdős Problem 732)

nodes.summary: The statement that there are a real number $c > 0$ and a natural number $N$ such that for every $n \ge N$ there is a finite set of at least $\exp(c \sqrt{n} \log n)$ distinct finite sequences of natural numbers, each of which is block-compatible for $n$. Here $\log$ is the natural logarithm.
nodes.title: Many block-compatible sequences

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, a finite list of blocks $B_1, \ldots, B_m \subseteq \{0, \ldots, n - 1\}$ is a pairwise balanced design on these $n$ points when the blocks are pairwise distinct, every block has at least two points, and every two distinct points lie in exactly one common block.
nodes.title: Pairwise balanced design
